name: Japan
targetIntake: September or October 2027 — Japan's autumn intake (May 2027 IB session)
tagline: A named minority route, on a calendar built for it
summary: Japan has a small, deliberate set of fully English-taught bachelor's degrees, and the IB Diploma is one of the qualifications they were built to receive. The University of Tokyo's PEAK has closed; its new English-taught College of Design opens in September 2027 and names the IB first. Around it sit Waseda's six English-based schools, Keio's PEARL, Sophia, ICU, Kyoto's iUP, Tohoku's new Gateway College, APU and Akita. The Japanese year starts in April, so the September and October intakes exist mainly for international applicants — which is why they fit a May 2027 IB session, and why every deadline falls between October 2026 and April 2027, before results.
whyConsider: The University of Tokyo opens a new English-taught faculty in September 2027 — its first new undergraduate faculty in about seventy years — with 50 of its 100 places on a route built for international qualifications and the IB named first.

Keio's PEARL runs three application periods for September 2027, the last closing on 7 April 2027, and accepts predicted IB grades in as many words. It is the latest Japanese deadline on this page and the one that fits a Danish school year.

Waseda's application window for September entry ran 8 January to 10 February in the most recent cycle — one application covering six English-based schools, late enough that predicted grades are settled.

Kyoto's iUP takes you with no Japanese at all: a six-month preparatory course, then four years of undergraduate study, 4.5 years in total, with fee waivers and monthly scholarships for eligible students.
National-university tuition in Japan is low by global standards, and private universities are far cheaper than their US or UK equivalents — though the 2027 figures are not confirmed here.

Money at the point of admission rather than by separate application: Waseda states that its scholarship recipients are determined by the admission result with no separate form, and Kyoto's iUP attaches fee waivers and monthly scholarships to eligible students. This matters more here than MEXT does, because the MEXT undergraduate scholarship is not offered to Danish nationals and depends, for everyone else, on the Japanese embassy in their country of citizenship — see the watch-outs.
Several programmes — ICU, Akita International University, APU — are built entirely around a bilingual liberal-arts model that maps naturally onto the IB's breadth.
watchOuts: The University of Tokyo's PEAK has ended — its own site states that September 2026 was the final student recruitment — but Todai has not closed to English-speaking school-leavers. The UTokyo College of Design opens in September 2027 and its applications close on 5 November 2026, the earliest Japanese deadline recorded here. It is a five-year integrated bachelor's and master's programme, not a bachelor's degree.
UTokyo's other English route, the Global Science Course, is a third-year transfer programme requiring at least two years of undergraduate study outside Japan. It is not an entry point from gymnasium.

Tohoku's Future Global Leadership courses and Sophia's Green Science and Green Engineering courses took their last students in 2026. Tohoku replaces FGL with Gateway College (English-taught, October 2027 intake, applications 15 December 2026 to 14 January 2027); Sophia opens an English-taught Bachelor of Engineering in Digital Green Technology.

Deadlines are a major trap, and they are spread over six months with nothing joining them up: UTokyo College of Design closes 5 November 2026, Kyoto iUP 3 December, Kyushu 11 December, Tohoku Gateway College 14 January 2027, Keio PEARL in three periods between December 2026 and 7 April 2027, Waseda at a date not yet announced. Build the list in the autumn of 2026.

Two intakes means two calendars, and neither is September by default. The Japanese academic year runs April to March; April 2027 entry would mean applying in mid-2026 and is not realistic. Kyoto's iUP enrols in October, which is a third calendar again.

MEXT is not what it looks like from Europe. The undergraduate scholarship funds a year of preparatory Japanese followed by a degree taught in Japanese; English-medium study happens only through 'direct placement', which MEXT decides, and MEXT chooses your university with no objection allowed.

Which embassy handles MEXT depends on your nationality: MEXT tells applicants to ask "the Japanese Embassy or Consulate General in your country". If you hold Danish citizenship, the undergraduate scholarship is not open to you. The Embassy of Japan in Denmark's Study in Japan page (dated 3 December 2020) lists two MEXT types for Danish nationals, Japanese Studies and Research Student, both for students already at university. Its 2026 news list carries a single MEXT call, for Research Students 2027. For any other nationality, ask the Japanese embassy in that country whether it runs the undergraduate track. Either way, plan Japan's finances around institutional awards and JASSO, and get the embassy's answer in writing before you build a year around MEXT.

The only official tuition figure quoted here is the University of Tokyo's own, and it carries no price year. The fee table linked from Japan's official study-promotion site is drawn from the Student Guide to Japan 2019–2020 and is out of date by several years.

If you can claim Danish SU, it does not follow you to Japan on the same terms as to an EU/EEA country. Check with su.dk early; a full degree outside the EU/EEA has separate rules. If you cannot claim it, check whether your own country's student finance covers a degree outside Europe.
Japanese universities generally want documents apostilled and sometimes notarised, and a Certificate of Eligibility must be obtained before the student visa. Start three months before travel.

ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: There is no national rule. Each English-taught programme treats the full IB Diploma as meeting the twelve-year schooling condition and sets its own standard on top. The UTokyo College of Design is the one that publishes a number: it expects 38 of 42 points across the six subjects plus at least 2 for TOK and the Extended Essay, and says expectations 'are not cut off scores'. Keio's PEARL and Tohoku's Gateway College accept an IB Diploma or predicted grades.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: No national conversion table. Each university reads IB points directly.
notes: The IB Diploma is one of the qualifications Japan's English-taught programmes were explicitly designed to receive, alongside A-levels, the US high school diploma plus SAT/ACT, and the Abitur.

Predicted grades do the work. Every September or October 2027 decision recorded here is made before 6 July 2027. Keio and Tohoku accept predictions in so many words; the UTokyo College of Design accepts a certified predicted score from anyone whose exams fall after its deadline, makes the offer conditional, and wants final results by 16 August 2027.

MEXT's scholarship route applies its own academic condition — twelve years of schooling completed by March of the arrival year, or by August where the applicant enters in the autumn term through direct placement. An IB Diploma completed in May sits between the two. For Danish nationals this is a secondary question, because the Embassy of Japan in Denmark does not offer them the undergraduate scholarship; for other nationalities it depends on the Japanese embassy in that country.
Some programmes also want SAT/ACT or a national university entrance examination for international students (EJU). Check each one — the requirements are not uniform.
The only published IB score found is the UTokyo College of Design's expectation of 38/42 plus 2 core points, which it says is not a cut-off. No other programme on this page publishes a minimum.

portal.name: No central portal — apply direct to each university

deadlines.label: UTokyo College of Design, Route B, September 2027 entry
deadlines.notes: Opens 15 October 2026 at 09:00 JST. Route B is the international-qualifications route (50 of the 100 places) and lists the IB. A separate video assignment is due 13–16 November 2026, first screening result 22 December 2026, final decision 20 February 2027. With predicted grades the offer is conditional and final results are due by 16 August 2027.

deadlines.label: Keio PEARL, Period III, September 2027 entry
deadlines.notes: The last of three periods sharing about 100 places; Periods I and II close 2 December 2026 and 27 January 2027. Result 24 May 2027 — after the examination session, before results. Keio accepts predicted IB grades explicitly. Application fee JPY 35,000.

deadlines.label: Waseda English-based undergraduate programmes, September 2027 entry
deadlines.notes: One application window covering the School of Political Science and Economics, School of Social Sciences, SILS, School of Culture Media and Society, and the two Science and Engineering schools. As of 23 September 2026 the only window published is 8 January to 10 February 2026, labelled for September 2026 entry. Check Waseda's page for the 2027 dates.

deadlines.label: Kyoto University iUP, October 2027 enrolment
deadlines.notes: Applications open 2 November 2026. Kyoto's own Apply page gives the period as "November 2 until December 3, 2026 (5 p.m. Japan Standard Time)". Screening stages and result dates are in Kyoto's guidelines PDF.

deadlines.label: Kyushu University international undergraduate programmes, October 2027 entry
deadlines.notes: A five-day window: the online application system is open only from 7 to 11 December 2026, so do not plan to start the form on the 11th. Kyushu then wants "all the necessary documents by post" as well. For the English-taught engineering programmes and Bioresource and Bioenvironment. No closing time is stated.

deadlines.label: Tohoku University Gateway College, October 2027 entry
deadlines.notes: Application period 15 December 2026 to 14 January 2027; first-stage result 5 February, second stage 21–22 February, successful applicants announced 24 March 2027. Predicted IB scores are accepted. No closing time is stated.

deadlines.label: University of Tokyo PEAK
deadlines.notes: Closed permanently. PEAK's announcement page states: "The Admission for September 2026 Enrollment will be the last student recruitment for the PEAK." PEAK's front page puts it in the past tense — "the applications for September 2026 enrollment are now closed", "this was the final student recruitment for PEAK, and no further applications will be accepted". Its successor is not a replacement PEAK but the UTokyo College of Design, which is listed above.

deadlines.label: MEXT Embassy Recommendation, undergraduate

readerAccess.reason: Depends on your nationality: you apply through the Japanese embassy in your country of citizenship, and each decides what it offers.

deadlines.notes: No undergraduate MEXT call appears on the Embassy of Japan in Denmark’s site: its news list for the whole of 2026 carries exactly one MEXT call, for Research Students, with an application deadline of 15 June 2026. MEXT’s national rule — recruitment in April and May of the year before arrival — therefore describes a window a Danish national cannot use through this embassy. If you hold another citizenship, the embassy track runs through the Embassy of Japan in your country of citizenship — check its own call for that window. Because this rests on what the embassy's site does not list, write to the embassy at info@ch.mofa.go.jp before relying on it either way. The route that plausibly remains open to a school-leaver is university-recommendation MEXT, after admission.

steps: In September 2026, build a spreadsheet of every English-taught programme you are interested in, with its intake month and its own deadline. There is no central portal and no shared calendar.
Decide April or September. For an IB student finishing in May 2027, September or October 2027 is the only realistic entry.
Ask your IB coordinator for predicted grades early — most Japanese applications are decided on predictions, an essay, a transcript and references.
Check whether each programme wants SAT/ACT or the EJU on top of the IB. If it does, book the test by autumn 2026.
Submit direct to each university through its own online portal, paying a separate application fee each time.

Do not build a MEXT application into the plan without checking first. If you hold Danish citizenship: the Embassy of Japan in Copenhagen offers Danish nationals only the Japanese Studies and Research Student types, both of which require you to be at university already, and ran no undergraduate call in 2026. Ask info@ch.mofa.go.jp directly. If you hold another citizenship, check the MEXT call of the Japanese embassy in your country of citizenship. The route that is open to a school-leaver is university-recommendation MEXT, which the university nominates you for after admitting you — so ask each admissions office whether it holds quota places.
Once you hold an offer, the university applies for your Certificate of Eligibility. You then take that to the Japanese embassy for the student visa. Allow three months.
application.selectionNotes: Selection is document-based and often interview-based rather than exam-based for English-taught programmes: transcript, predicted grades, personal statement, references and sometimes an online interview. This suits IB students who write well. The competitive bar at Kyoto, Waseda's Political Science and Economics, and Keio is high; APU, Akita and several regional programmes are more accessible.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Limited but real: a few dozen fully English-taught bachelor's programmes nationally, concentrated at Waseda (six schools), Keio, Sophia, ICU, Kyoto, Tohoku, Kyushu, Nagoya, Tsukuba, Hokkaido, APU and Akita. The UTokyo College of Design opens in September 2027; PEAK, Tohoku's FGL and Sophia's Green Science and Engineering courses have closed. No national total is given here.
language.englishProof: Set per programme, usually as a test. The UTokyo College of Design and Tohoku's Gateway College both want TOEFL iBT 80, IELTS 6.0, Duolingo 110 or Cambridge 169 or more; Keio PEARL wants TOEFL iBT or IELTS Academic. Whether an IB English A or B result replaces the test is not confirmed at any of them, so ask.
notes: Kyoto iUP explicitly states that Japanese proficiency is not required at the outset — the six-month preparatory course exists to build it.
No English-taught programme requires Japanese to enrol, but essentially all of them require you to study it, and you will need it for part-time work, housing and daily life.
APU and ICU are formally bilingual: you take courses in both languages as your Japanese improves.

tuitionEuEea.value: Japan charges the same tuition to all nationalities — there is no EU/non-EU split.

costs.applicationFee: Charged separately by each university. Keio PEARL: JPY 35,000 for September 2027 entry. Check the others on each university's page.
notes: The University of Tokyo publishes an admission fee of 282,000 yen once and tuition of 642,960 yen a year. The page states no academic year and says nothing about the new College of Design. Todai has raised its tuition above the national standard of 535,800 yen, which is the reason not to quote a national figure for any particular Japanese university.

The fee table linked from Japan's own official study-promotion site is drawn from the Student Guide to Japan 2019–2020 and converts at 114 yen to the dollar. It is the first thing an English-speaking applicant lands on and it should not be used for a 2027 or 2028 budget.

The structure to expect: national universities charge a one-off admission fee plus an annual tuition fee, both set nationally. Private universities (Waseda, Keio, Sophia, ICU, APU) charge considerably more and vary by faculty, with science and engineering highest.
Budget separately for the admission fee, which is charged once and is substantial, and for compulsory facility or lab fees at private universities.
Tokyo living costs are high; Beppu (APU), Akita and Sendai (Tohoku) are dramatically cheaper.

funding: MEXT (Monbukagakusho) Undergraduate Scholarship — nationally this is five years from April, one of them a preparatory year in Japanese, 117,000 yen a month, entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees waived, and an economy air ticket each way, with all classes in Japanese except where a grantee is directly placed at a university requiring none, and with MEXT rather than the student choosing the university. It is listed because people ask about it, not because it is available: the Embassy of Japan in Copenhagen lists only two MEXT types for Danish nationals, Japanese Studies and Research Student, and neither is this one. On a Danish passport, from a Danish gymnasium, treat the embassy track as closed until the embassy tells you otherwise in writing.

University-recommendation MEXT places — some universities nominate their own admitted students, and for a Danish national this is the only MEXT route that plausibly remains open, since it runs through the university rather than the embassy; other nationals may also have their own embassy's track. Ask each admissions office whether it holds MEXT quota places and how a new international entrant is considered for one.
JASSO Honors Scholarship — a monthly grant administered by the Japan Student Services Organization for privately financed international students. Check the current amount with JASSO.

Institutional awards decided at admission: Waseda states that recipients of its scholarships are determined by the admission result with no separate application, and that its awards are grants rather than loans.
APU operates tuition-reduction scholarships awarded at admission at several percentage levels — check the current levels with APU.
Kyoto iUP offers admission and tuition fee waivers plus monthly scholarships to eligible students.

funding.note: A full degree outside the EU/EEA follows separate rules, with its own ties-to-Denmark form: check su.dk before budgeting.

workRights: Students with College Student (留学) status may work up to 28 hours a week once they hold a blanket Permission to Engage in Activity Other Than That Permitted (Immigration Services Agency). Check the rules for longer hours in the official long vacations with your university.
residency: Non-visa-waiver process regardless of EU citizenship. The university applies for a Certificate of Eligibility on your behalf once you accept an offer; you then take it to the Embassy of Japan in Copenhagen for a Student visa. On arrival you receive a residence card and must register at the local municipal office within 14 days and enrol in National Health Insurance.
housing: Most English-taught programmes guarantee or strongly prioritise first-year places in a university dormitory or international house, which is by far the easiest route and usually cheaper than the private market. APU houses all first-year international students in AP House. Private renting in Japan involves key money, guarantor requirements and agency fees that are difficult to navigate from abroad — take the dormitory.
healthcare: Enrolment in Japan's National Health Insurance is compulsory for anyone staying more than three months and is arranged at the municipal office when you register. It covers roughly 70% of medical costs; students typically add the university's own supplementary cover. Your EHIC does not apply in Japan.

institutions.name: University of Tokyo
institutions.englishBachelors: The UTokyo College of Design, opening September 2027: a five-year integrated bachelor's and master's programme taught in English, 100 places, half of them on Route B for international qualifications including the IB (expected level 38/42 plus 2 core points, not a cut-off). PEAK closed after its September 2026 intake. The Global Science Course is a third-year transfer route, not an entry point from school.
institutions.note: PEAK has closed, and the English-taught College of Design opens in its place in September 2027. It is Todai's first new undergraduate faculty in about seventy years, on a September intake with half its places on the international route; applications close on 5 November 2026.

institutions.name: Kyoto University
institutions.englishBachelors: iUP — a 4.5-year route: six months of intensive preparatory Japanese, then four years of undergraduate study across a range of faculties. No Japanese required at the start.
institutions.note: iUP takes you with no Japanese at the start, with fee waivers and monthly scholarships on offer. Guidelines for October 2027 enrolment were published in July 2026.

institutions.name: Waseda University
institutions.englishBachelors: Six schools: Political Science and Economics, Social Sciences, International Liberal Studies (SILS), Culture Media and Society, Fundamental Science and Engineering, Creative Science and Engineering. SILS and Culture Media and Society also take April entrants.
institutions.note: Six English-based schools under one application window, which ran 8 January to 10 February in the last cycle, late enough for settled predicted grades. Scholarships are decided from the admission result with no separate application.

institutions.name: Keio University
institutions.englishBachelors: PEARL (Programme in Economics for Alliances, Research and Leadership) in the Faculty of Economics — about 100 places, entry 22 September 2027, three application periods closing 2 December 2026, 27 January 2027 and 7 April 2027, accepting an IB Diploma or predicted grades with TOEFL iBT or IELTS. GIGA (Global Information and Governance Academic) in Environment and Information Studies at Shonan Fujisawa is not covered in detail here.
institutions.note: Japan's oldest private university and Waseda's historic rival. PEARL is an English-medium economics degree; GIGA is a technology-and-policy hybrid on the Shonan Fujisawa campus.

institutions.name: Sophia University
institutions.englishBachelors: Faculty of Liberal Arts (BA in Liberal Arts); the Sophia Program for Sustainable Futures (BAs in Journalism, Education, Sociology, Economics, Management, International Relations and Area Studies); and a Bachelor of Engineering in Digital Green Technology. The Green Science and Green Engineering courses admitted their last students in autumn 2026.
institutions.note: A Jesuit university in central Tokyo whose Faculty of Liberal Arts has taught entirely in English since the 1940s. Small, central and internationally minded.

institutions.name: Tohoku University
institutions.englishBachelors: Gateway College, new in 2027: an English-taught undergraduate programme with a Humanities and Social Sciences track and a STEM track, taking about 90 students in October and 88 in April. It replaces the Future Global Leadership (FGL) courses, which admitted their last students in 2026.
institutions.note: A national research university in Sendai, a comfortable city far cheaper than Tokyo. Gateway College applications for October 2027 run 15 December 2026 to 14 January 2027, and it accepts predicted IB scores.

institutions.name: International Christian University
institutions.englishBachelors: A single bilingual Bachelor of Arts in Liberal Arts with 31 majors; you declare your major at the end of second year. Entry is possible in April or September.
institutions.note: A small liberal-arts college on a wooded campus in western Tokyo: one degree, 31 majors, taught bilingually. Declaring your major late suits an IB student who is not yet sure.

institutions.name: Ritsumeikan Asia Pacific University
institutions.englishBachelors: Three colleges, all offering fully English-taught degrees: Asia Pacific Studies (APS), International Management (APM, AACSB-accredited) and Sustainability and Tourism (ST). April and September intakes.
institutions.note: About half the student body is international, from ninety-odd countries. Beppu is a hot-spring town on Kyushu, cheap and beautiful but remote; tuition-reduction scholarships are awarded at admission.

institutions.name: Akita International University
institutions.englishBachelors: All teaching is in English. One undergraduate degree programme with three courses: Global Business, Global Studies and Global Connectivity. April and September intakes. A year abroad is compulsory for every student.
institutions.note: A small public university in northern Japan where every class is in English. Every student spends a year at a partner university abroad, and it is known for its 24-hour library and strong graduate employment.

institutions.name: Kyushu University
institutions.englishBachelors: International undergraduate programmes taught in English, October entry: engineering (several departments) and Bioresource and Bioenvironment in the School of Agriculture. Applications for October 2027 run 7–11 December 2026.
institutions.note: A large national university in Fukuoka, the big Japanese city closest to the Asian mainland. It teaches engineering and bioresource programmes in English.

institutions.name: University of Tsukuba
institutions.englishBachelors: Several English-taught bachelor's programmes, including the Bachelor's Program in Global Issues and the Bachelor's Program in Interdisciplinary Engineering.
institutions.note: In Japan's purpose-built science city, an hour north of Tokyo, among many research institutes. Strong in sport science.

institutions.name: Temple University, Japan Campus
institutions.englishBachelors: All undergraduate degrees are taught in English — it is an American university operating in Tokyo, awarding a US Temple University degree.
institutions.note: An American university's campus on a purpose-built site in Sangenjaya. Useful if you want an American-style degree and the option to transfer to Philadelphia, but it charges American tuition.

institutions.name: Hokkaido University
institutions.englishBachelors: Two English-taught undergraduate programmes: the Integrated Science Program (ISP) in the natural sciences, and the Modern Japanese Studies Program (MJSP), which starts with a six-month intensive Japanese course in October.
institutions.note: Founded on an American land-grant model and strong in agriculture, fisheries and cold-region science. Sapporo is spacious and snowy.

institutions.name: Nagoya University
institutions.englishBachelors: The G30 International Programs, October entry: Automotive Engineering, Physics, Chemistry, Biological Science, Social Science (law and economics) and Japan-in-Asia Cultural Studies. The 2027 admission requirements were published in August 2026.
institutions.note: Six English-taught G30 degrees in the middle of Japan's car industry, Toyota's home region. Six Nobel laureates in the sciences since 2000.

institutions.name: The University of Osaka
institutions.englishBachelors: Two English-taught undergraduate degrees: the Human Sciences International Undergraduate Degree Program and the International Undergraduate Program in Science (which replaced the Chemistry-Biology Combined Major).
institutions.note: A large research university known for immunology and robotics, now using the English name The University of Osaka. Its English-taught offer is two programmes, so check each carefully before counting on it.
